passage: Baby Jagdish wailed in his cot, and five-year-old Madhuri hurried over, patted his tummy and ran to call "Mummy!" Her mother, Uma, thanked her. "You fetched me so fast, and your patting helped him." Madhuri felt big and needed. But when Jagdish cried during her drawing time, Uma ran to him again and forgot the drawing altogether. Madhuri felt forgotten. She dropped her crayons, crawled on the floor and said in a baby voice, "Me baby too." Uma did not scold. That evening she said, "I need a helper to carry the nappy bag, and after Jagdish sleeps, it is our time: two stories." Madhuri fetched the bag proudly. On Saturday, when Jagdish cried again, she brought a rattle without being asked. "Thank you, love. You brought the rattle, and now he is looking at it," Uma said. "But you are not his little mother; that is my job. Come and sit with me." Madhuri leaned against her, content.

qa.q: What did Madhuri do when baby Jagdish wailed in his cot?
qa.a: She patted his tummy and ran to call Mummy.

qa.q: How did Uma respond when Madhuri helped with Jagdish, compared with when Madhuri said "Me baby too"?
qa.a: When Madhuri patted Jagdish and fetched her, Uma thanked her for those specific things; when Madhuri crawled and used a baby voice, Uma did not scold but gave her the nappy bag to carry and promised two stories after Jagdish slept.

qa.q: What was Madhuri feeling when she said "Me baby too"?
qa.a: She felt forgotten and a little jealous, wanting to be looked after like the baby.

qa.q: What could Uma keep doing to help Madhuri feel seen without making her a permanent little parent?
qa.a: She could keep the helper jobs and special story time, thank Madhuri for specific actions, and remind her that looking after Jagdish is a grown-up job.

grounding: One big sister shows caring, feeling forgotten, wanting to be a baby again and proud protectiveness when a baby brother cries, with a mother responding to each.
